entities.name: Uurad
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Uurad, or Ferat son of Bargoit, was a Pictish king who ruled from 839 to 842 CE.

As the last king of the Picts before the rise of the Kingdom of Alba, Uurad's reign marked the end of Pictish dominance in Scotland and the beginning of a new era of integration with the surrounding Celtic kingdoms.

The Battle of Invernahavon in 842 CE, fought during Uurad's reign, was a decisive victory for the Kingdom of Alba, cementing its position as the dominant power in Scotland.

Uurad's legacy extends beyond his own kingdom, as he played a key role in the development of the Kingdom of Alba's laws and institutions, which would go on to shape the history of Scotland for centuries to come.

The Pictish Chronicle, a 10th-century manuscript that records Uurad's reign, contains a striking quote: "Uurad, son of Bargoit, was a just and fair king, beloved by his people."
